given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today
given.why: Two loans are lent on 2026-03-02, so they're due 2026-03-16, and the job runs on 2026-03-17.
The test clock is always set to 10:00Z, so no test runs near midnight, and a job that worked out 'today' in local time would still pass.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The database is fresh and has no reminders when the job runs.

then.why: The fake's `sent` list must hold exactly the two reminders, so a job that never asks would fail.
Each sent reminder must carry the lending member's `memberId` along with its `loanId`.
The order only shows when the API refuses. B3's test asserts that a refused loan has no row in `reminders`, so recording before asking would fail there.
The `reminders` table must hold exactly one row for each loan.
`sent_on` must be 2026-03-17, the run date, not the due date 2026-03-16.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice on the same day, so loan1 already has a reminder recorded today on the second run.
loan2 is overdue but returned before the job runs.
copy-3 is added to the catalogue but never lent, so no open loan that isn't yet overdue exists, and the boundary case of `dueOn` equal to today is never set up.

then.why: Because `toMatchObject` on an array also checks its length, it would catch a second reminder to loan1 or one to the returned loan2. With no loan that isn't overdue, though, a job that also reminds loans due today (`<=` instead of `<`) would still pass.

given.why: The fake refuses loan1 with 'Notifications API answered 503'.
B5's test proves that a failed connection comes back as a refusal, the same result the job handles in this row's test.

then.why: The `reminders` table must equal exactly loan2's row, so a row for loan1 would fail.
The exact event name is asserted with `toContainEqual`.
The level must be `warn` for the entry to match.
`fields.loanId` must equal loan1's ID exactly.
`fields.error` must equal the fake's refusal reason exactly.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: The refused loan1 is due a day earlier than loan2, and loan2 must still be sent and recorded, so stopping after the refusal would fail.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are set up, one of them refused, and the job runs to completion.

then.why: The last log entry must have exactly this event name.
The level must be `info`.
`sent` must equal 2.
`failed` must equal 1, and `toEqual` rules out extra fields.

given.why: Every test sends a fixed reminder through the real client.

then.why: The recorded method must be POST, and the handler only matches `http.post`.
The path must be `/notifications`, and the interceptor errors on any unhandled request (tests/support/http-interceptor.setup.ts:4), which pins the host to NOTIFY_URL.
The content-type must be exactly `application/json`, and the body is parsed with `request.json()`.
The whole body is compared with `toEqual`, so a renamed or missing key would fail.
The exact template value is asserted.
The exact keys and values inside `data` are asserted.
Answers of 200, 202 and 204 must each give `accepted`, so checking only for 200 would fail.
A 400 must give `refused`, so treating only 5xx as refused would fail. No 3xx answer is tested.
`HttpResponse.error()` must give `refused` rather than an exception.

then.part: with a reason naming the status
then.why: The reason must contain '400'.

then.part: or saying the API was unreachable
then.why: The reason must contain 'unreachable'.
